M/S.Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance ... vs Chatla Laxmi And
Anr on 21 July, 2023
Author: Lalitha Kanneganti

Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.254 of 2009
Judgment:

Aggrieved by the award and decree dated 25-01-2007 in O.P.No.830 of 2004 on the file of the Chairman, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge(FTC),
Adilabad (for short, 'the Tribunal'), the Insurance Company filed this appeal.

entities.text:
Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-II Additional District Judge(FTC),
Adilabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Having heard both sides, perused the entire material on record.
3. The case of the claimant is that he is aged about 22 years and was a student of B.S.C.

On 01.11.2004, while the deceased was unloading the kirana shop articles from the standing jeep by the side of the road, a lorry came from Adilabad side driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased and he sustained fracture of both legs, fatal injuries to head and other parts of the body.
Later he succumbed to the said injuries.
Police registered a case i.e., Crime No.85 of 2004.
LK, J MACMA_254_2009 4.
The Claim petition is filed by the Mother of the deceased claiming compensation of an amount of Rs.3,00,000/-.
The tribunal considering the income at Rs.2,000/- per month has granted the compensation of an amount of Rs. 3,02,000/-.
5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that the tribunal has taken the age of the deceased as 22 years and as per the PME report the age of the deceased is 35 years.
It is submitted that the tribunal ought to have taken the age of the deceased as 35 years.
In view of the same, the multiplier that is applied is also not correct.
It is submitted that the tribunal ought not to have taken Rs.2,000/- as Income.
It is submitted that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal was excessive.

6. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent/claimant submits that though the claimant has not filed any appeal or cross objections still as the Insurance Company has questioned the quantum and while considering the same if this Court comes to a conclusion that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable, this Court without there being an appeal or cross objection can as well enhance the LK, J MACMA_254_2009 compensation.

sentences.text: the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is a beneficial legislation.
7. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the deceased was pursuing his B.S.C. and the tribunal has taken only Rs.2,000/- as income.
He also submits that the Hon'ble Apex Court in recent judgment has held that even in case of 10th class student income has to be taken as Rs.10,000/-.
Hence the Income may be considered as Rs.10,000/- and the amount may be enhanced.
It is submitted that even under the other heads also the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal was not reasonable.
8. In this Case, first coming to the age of the claimant, as per the PME report, his age is 35 years.
The Tribunal has considered the age as 22 years.
As per the PMA report, this Court is inclined to consider the age as 35 years.

Then coming to the Income for computing the compensation as he is pursuing his B.S.C. 1st year, in case of B.S.C. graduate student, the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Ramulamma and LK, J MACMA_254_2009 others v. Venkatesh Bus Union and another1 has held that for final year student the income was taken as Rs.12,000/- and for 1st year student it is taken as Rs.10,000/-.

entities.text: Ramulamma and LK, J MACMA_254_2009 others v. Venkatesh Bus Union
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the same, this Court is inclined to consider the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/-.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2 held that while considering the compensation in cases of death, the future prospects of the self employed shall also be considered.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having regard to the age and occupation as self-employed, if 40 percent of the income is included as future prospects, the monthly income would come to Rs.8,400/-.
As per his age i.e. 31 years as on the date of accident, the appropriate multiplier would be '16'.
Since the deceased was a bachelor, his personal and living expenses shall be deducted at 50% which comes to Rs.4,200/-.
Hence, the claimant is entitled to Rs.8,06,400/- (Rs.4,200x12x16) for loss of annual future income due to death of the deceased.

As there is one claimant, she is entitled to Rs.44,000/-
towards loss of consortium.
As the Tribunal has granted very meager amount towards funeral expenses, this Court is inclined to grant Rs.33,000/- towards funeral expenses and loss of estate and Rs.10,000/- for legal expenses.

10. In the light of the above discussion, the claimants are entitled for the following compensation under different heads:
 Heads

Compensation awarded (1) Loss of consortium Rs.44,000/-
(2) Funeral Expenses Rs.33,000/-
(3) Loss of dependency Rs.8,06,400/-
(4) Legal Expenses Rs.10,000/-

Total compensation awarded Rs.8,93,400/-

LK, J MACMA_254_2009 (a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(b) The claimant shall pay the court fee on the enhanced amount of compensation.
(c) The insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of (8) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of judgment.
On such deposit, claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing the security.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
